meta.title: Thermostatic valve (TRV): quick start
meta.description: Control your Zigbee thermostatic valves (Sonoff TRVZB...) with Versatile Thermostat: direct valve control, external sensor, Auto-TPI and central boiler.

trv.name: Thermostatic valve
trv.tagline: Zigbee thermostatic heads on hot-water radiators.
trv.title: Thermostatic valve (TRV)
trv.intro: A thermostatic head measures the temperature right next to the radiator, so it regulates poorly. Versatile Thermostat recalibrates it against a real room sensor and can directly control the valve opening.
trv.vtherm_type: “Thermostat over a climate” (over_climate) with self-regulation by direct valve control. For valves that don't expose their opening, use light or medium self-regulation.

valve_regulation.title: Direct valve control
valve_regulation.desc: Versatile Thermostat computes the opening percentage with the TPI algorithm and sends it to the valve, instead of juggling its setpoint.

external_sensor.title: Room sensor and calibration
external_sensor.desc: The room temperature comes from a real sensor. It can be copied into the valve (calibration offset or external temperature).

auto_tpi.title: Auto-TPI
auto_tpi.desc: Regulation coefficients are learned automatically over successive cycles, room by room.

window.title: Open windows
window.desc: Valves close when a window opens, via a sensor or automatic detection of the temperature drop.

central_boiler.title: Central boiler
central_boiler.desc: The boiler switches on when enough valves call for heat and switches off when all of them are closed.

multi.title: Several valves per room
multi.desc: A single thermostat controls all the valves in a room, with a minimum and maximum opening per valve.

tutorial.title: Tutorial: a living room with two Sonoff TRVZB
tutorial.example: Example: a living room heated by two hot-water radiators, each fitted with a Sonoff TRVZB paired through Zigbee2MQTT, and a Zigbee temperature sensor in the middle of the room.
tutorial.tip: With the Sonoff TRVZB, keep a regulation threshold of at least 3%: below that, the valve may lose its calibration. If that happens, use the valve recalibration service.

pair.title: Pair the valves and the sensor
pair.text: Pair both valves and the sensor in Zigbee2MQTT. Check that each valve exposes the number entities “valve opening degree”, “valve closing degree” and “local temperature calibration”.

install.title: Install Versatile Thermostat
install.text: Install the integration from HACS, then restart Home Assistant.

create.title: Create the thermostat
create.text: Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > Versatile Thermostat. Choose “Thermostat over a climate”, name it “Living room” and select the temperature sensor.

underlying.title: Add the valves
underlying.text: In “Underlyings”, add the two valve climate entities.

regulation.title: Enable direct valve control
regulation.text: In “Self-regulation”, choose direct valve control. For each valve, fill in the opening, closing and calibration entities. Leave the TPI coefficients at their defaults: Auto-TPI will tune them.

presets.title: Set the presets
presets.text: Define the Eco, Comfort, Boost and Frost protection temperatures, for example 18, 20, 21 and 7 °C.

features.title: Windows and boiler
features.text: Enable open window detection (sensor or automatic). If a boiler feeds the radiators, declare it in the central configuration so it follows the valves' demand.

meta.title: Pilot wire electric radiator: quick start
meta.description: Control pilot wire electric radiators (Nodon, Heatzy, relay + diode) with Versatile Thermostat: TPI algorithm, power shedding, presence and windows.
meta.keywords: pilot wire,fil pilote,electric radiator,Nodon,Heatzy,power shedding,Home Assistant,Versatile Thermostat

pilot_wire.name: Electric pilot wire
pilot_wire.tagline: Electric radiators driven by pilot wire or relay.
pilot_wire.title: Pilot wire electric radiator
pilot_wire.intro: The pilot wire (fil pilote) only understands a few orders: Comfort, Eco, Frost protection, off. Versatile Thermostat turns it into precise regulation, alternating Comfort and Frost protection at the right pace thanks to the TPI algorithm.
pilot_wire.vtherm_type: “Thermostat over a switch” (over_switch). The underlying device can be a relay, a select entity (pilot wire module) or a climate (Heatzy) driven by custom commands.

pilot_wire.title: Every pilot wire module
pilot_wire.desc: Nodon, Heatzy or relay + diode: custom commands send the right order (Comfort / Frost protection) and the “Invert command” option handles diode wiring.

tpi.title: TPI algorithm
tpi.desc: On each cycle, Versatile Thermostat computes the heating time from the gap to the setpoint and the outdoor temperature: the room stays stable to a tenth of a degree.

power_shedding.title: Power shedding
power_shedding.desc: Radiators are cut by priority when consumption approaches your subscribed power. Start-ups are staggered to smooth out current peaks.

presence_motion.title: Presence and motion
presence_motion.desc: Heating automatically lowers when you're away and returns to Comfort as soon as motion is detected.

window.title: Open windows
window.desc: The radiator switches off when a window opens, with or without a sensor.

central_mode.title: Centralized control
central_mode.desc: A single selector puts the whole home in Eco, Frost protection or off.

tutorial.title: Tutorial: a bedroom with a Nodon pilot wire module
tutorial.example: Example: a bedroom heated by an electric radiator wired to a Nodon SIN-4-FP-21 module, with a Zigbee temperature sensor and a window opening sensor.
tutorial.tip: On the radiator, set the internal setpoint above Versatile Thermostat's highest setpoint (24 °C for example): Versatile Thermostat does the regulating, so the radiator must not cut off before it does.

wiring.title: Wire the module
wiring.text: Wire the pilot wire module to the radiator and add it to Home Assistant. It exposes a select entity with the Comfort, Eco, Frost protection and off orders.

install.title: Install Versatile Thermostat
install.text: Install the integration from HACS, then restart Home Assistant.

create.title: Create the thermostat
create.text: Add the Versatile Thermostat integration, choose “Thermostat over a switch”, name it “Bedroom” and select the temperature sensor and the outdoor sensor.

underlying.title: Add the radiator
underlying.text: In “Underlyings”, select the module's select entity. Turn-on command: select_option/option:comfort. Turn-off command: select_option/option:frost_protection.

tpi.title: Set the cycle
tpi.text: Choose a cycle of 5 to 10 minutes and a minimum activation delay of 30 seconds. Keep the default TPI coefficients or enable Auto-TPI.

presets.title: Set the presets
presets.text: Define the Eco, Comfort, Boost and Frost protection temperatures, for example 17, 19, 20 and 7 °C.

features.title: Window and power shedding
features.text: Link the window opening sensor. In the central configuration, declare the home's power sensor and the maximum power to enable power shedding.

meta.title: Heat pump and air conditioning: quick start
meta.description: Regulate your air-to-air heat pump or air conditioner with Versatile Thermostat: self-regulation, automatic stop and restart, heating and cooling.
meta.keywords: heat pump,air conditioning,air-to-air heat pump,auto start stop,Home Assistant,Versatile Thermostat

heat_pump.name: Heat pump
heat_pump.tagline: Air-to-air heat pump or reversible air conditioner driven by Home Assistant.
heat_pump.title: Heat pump and air conditioning
heat_pump.intro: A heat pump measures the temperature at the indoor unit, often far from the reality of the room. Versatile Thermostat corrects its setpoint with a real sensor and stops it when it's no longer needed.
heat_pump.vtherm_type: “Thermostat over a climate” (over_climate), with cooling mode if your heat pump is reversible.

self_regulation.title: Self-regulation
self_regulation.desc: Versatile Thermostat adjusts the setpoint sent to the heat pump so the room sensor reaches the target temperature. Four levels, from light to expert.

auto_start_stop.title: Automatic stop and restart
auto_start_stop.desc: When the room is at temperature, the heat pump is stopped (or switched to fan or dehumidification) then restarted at the right time: less consumption and noise.

heat_cool.title: Heating and cooling
heat_cool.desc: The same thermostat heats in winter and cools in summer, with presets dedicated to cooling. Auto-Fan adapts the fan speed.

window.title: Open windows
window.desc: The heat pump stops or switches to fan mode when a window opens.

presence.title: Presence
presence.desc: Away setpoints apply automatically, for both heating and cooling.

power.title: Power shedding and central mode
power.desc: The heat pump takes part in power shedding. Central mode forces the whole home to heating only or cooling only.

tutorial.title: Tutorial: a living room with a Mitsubishi heat pump
tutorial.example: Example: a living room cooled by a Mitsubishi air-to-air heat pump integrated via MELCloud, with a temperature sensor placed far from the indoor unit.
tutorial.tip: Start with light self-regulation and raise the level only if the room doesn't reach its setpoint. Avoid aggressive settings with heat pumps that cut their compressor too often.

integration.title: Integrate the heat pump
integration.text: Add your heat pump's integration (MELCloud, Daikin, SmartIR...) in Home Assistant and check that its climate entity responds.

install.title: Install Versatile Thermostat
install.text: Install the integration from HACS, then restart Home Assistant.

create.title: Create the thermostat
create.text: Add the Versatile Thermostat integration, choose “Thermostat over a climate”, name it “Living room” and select the temperature sensor and the outdoor sensor.

underlying.title: Add the heat pump
underlying.text: In “Underlyings”, select the heat pump's climate entity and tick cooling mode if it is reversible.

regulation.title: Enable self-regulation
regulation.text: In “Self-regulation”, choose the light level. It corrects the setpoint sent to the heat pump by up to 1.5 °C.

auto_start_stop.title: Enable automatic stop and restart
auto_start_stop.text: Choose the responsiveness (slow for a living room, fast for a small room) and the stop action: turn off, fan only or dehumidification.

presets.title: Set the presets
presets.text: Define the heating temperatures (for example 18 / 20 / 21 °C) and the cooling temperatures (for example 26 / 25 / 24 °C).

meta.title: Pellet stove: quick start
meta.description: Regulate your pellet stove with Versatile Thermostat: dry contact or integration, suitable long cycles, presence, windows and failure detection.
meta.keywords: pellet stove,pellet heater,dry contact,Home Assistant,Versatile Thermostat

pellet_stove.name: Pellet stove
pellet_stove.tagline: Stove driven by dry contact, relay or dedicated integration.
pellet_stove.title: Pellet stove
pellet_stove.intro: A pellet stove doesn't tolerate repeated ignitions well: each start-up uses electricity and fouls the burn pot. Versatile Thermostat drives it with long cycles for stable comfort without multiplying ignitions.
pellet_stove.vtherm_type: “Thermostat over a switch” (over_switch) if the stove is controlled through its room thermostat dry contact via a relay. “Thermostat over a climate” (over_climate) if a Home Assistant integration exposes the stove as a climate.

long_cycle.title: Long cycles
long_cycle.desc: The cycle duration and the minimum on and off delays can be set to respect the stove's start-up time.

external_sensor.title: Room sensor
external_sensor.desc: Temperature is measured where you live, not next to the stove, which would otherwise overheat the main room.

auto_start_stop.title: Automatic stop and restart
auto_start_stop.desc: With a stove exposed as a climate, automatic stop and restart avoid leaving it idling when the room is at temperature.

presence.title: Presence
presence.desc: The stove switches to Eco when the home is empty and restores Comfort before you return.

window.title: Open windows
window.desc: The stove switches off when a window stays open.

failure_detection.title: Failure detection
failure_detection.desc: If the temperature doesn't rise while the stove is supposed to be heating (empty hopper, ignition fault), Versatile Thermostat flags it.

tutorial.title: Tutorial: a stove controlled by dry contact
tutorial.example: Example: a pellet stove with a “room thermostat” input (dry contact), wired to a Zigbee relay module, with a temperature sensor in the living room.
tutorial.tip: The pellet stove doesn't have a dedicated profile in the documentation yet: these settings are inspired by high-inertia heating. Adjust the cycle duration to your stove's manual and share your settings with the community.

control.title: Wire the dry contact
control.text: Wire the stove's room thermostat input to a relay integrated in Home Assistant, following the stove's manual. Configure the stove to obey this contact.

install.title: Install Versatile Thermostat
install.text: Install the integration from HACS, then restart Home Assistant.

create.title: Create the thermostat
create.text: Add the Versatile Thermostat integration, choose “Thermostat over a switch”, name it “Stove” and select the temperature sensor and the outdoor sensor.

underlying.title: Add the relay
underlying.text: In “Underlyings”, select the relay's switch entity.

cycle.title: Set a long cycle
cycle.text: Choose a long cycle (30 to 60 minutes) and minimum on and off delays of several minutes, so a start-up always runs to completion.

presets.title: Set the presets
presets.text: Define the Eco, Comfort, Boost and Frost protection temperatures, for example 18, 20, 21 and 10 °C.

features.title: Presence, windows and failure
features.text: Link the presence sensor and the window opening sensors, then enable heating failure detection to be alerted if the stove doesn't start.
